body: I don't think we should allow null here. This shouldn't be a problem, removing this default path configuration and the `translations/` directory will have the same effect.
Alternatively, you could set a fake default path config e.g. `'null'` or rename the `translations/` directory to anything else.

> Alternatively, you could set a fake default path config e.g. `'null'` or rename the `translations/` directory to anything else.

I currently set a fake default path. Maybe I will set it to the last value of `framework.translator.paths`. But it took some time to find out where the fatal error was coming from. Therefore I suggest to "report clearly the config value may not be null" by checking the validity somewhere in the call chain (probably in `FrameworkExtension::registerTranslatorConfiguration()`).

(I set
```
framework.translator.paths: [ '%kernel.project_dir%/translations', '%kernel.project_dir%/my-trans-overwrite-path/' ]
```
to let translations from my-trans-overwrite-path win over the default path. But then I must change default_path, because it is the strongest one.)

I have the same use case as the reporter for setting `framework.translator.default_path` to null. Setting a fake path is a sensible workaround but are you certain that won't break backwards compatibility at some point? I believe allowing null and letting the user set a specific order through `framework.translator.paths` is a much cleaner solution.
The problem already appears somewhen when upgrading some dependencies in symfony 3.4 (so already before symfony4, sorry for not knowing more exactly where it happens)

it's odd that the `default_path` actually overrides the values set in `paths`. That is not what I'd expect from something labelled _default_. It acts like it is at the last (most important) position in the list of `paths`, when it should be in the first. But since any behavior of `default_path` can be expressed using `paths `alone, why not just leave it off?

Generally it is irritating that the order in tranlations is totally different to the order from templates.

In translations, the last found entry wins (`default_path`, lower priority has last found in `paths`).
In templates, the first found template wins. (The first one found in paths, if none then fallback to default.) I agree that the name 'default' is misleading here.

Let's at least document clearly how it works (https://github.com/symfony/symfony-docs/pull/13430).
Totally changing the priority would probaly break BC hardly, so this is unrealistic.
But improvement is possible.

Hey, thanks for your report!
There has not been a lot of activity here for a while. Is this bug still relevant? Have you managed to find a workaround?
Just a quick reminder to make a comment on this. If I don't hear anything I'll close this.

Hey,

I didn't hear anything so I'm going to close it. Feel free to comment if this is still relevant, I can always reopen!

* `fileExists()` in https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/855aab2/src/Symfony/Component/DependencyInjection/ContainerBuilder.php#L389 did not change
* `$container->fileExists($defaultDir)` in https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/855aab2/src/Symfony/Bundle/FrameworkBundle/DependencyInjection/FrameworkExtension.php#L1283 does not check for `null == $defaultDir`
* this bug is not mentioned anywhere

So this strongly indicates that the bug is still open. (Not yet checked: test with newest symfony.)

issue.title: allow null for framework.translator.default_path
issue.body:
Allow to configure framework.translator.default_path to null, as it was until symfony 3.4.x (fix BC compatibility).
